$comment: [[D-C-PE64-CORPUS-BLOCKED-BY-AN-UNDECLARED-WIN32-CALL-AND-A-TYPE-DSS-SPLITS-THAT-MINGW-ALIASES]] (P66 lane pe). The two DECLARATION gaps that made `pe64-x86_64` the last poisoned leg of the SQLite matrix, as one runnable program. GAP 1: `windows.json` did not declare kernel32's `GetDriveTypeW` nor the winbase.h `DRIVE_*` family, so `os_win.c`'s aSyscall row and `osGetDriveTypeW(zRoot)==DRIVE_REMOTE` were the ONLY two `S_UndeclaredIdentifier` sites in the whole testfixture build. GAP 2: `sys/stat.json` declared `struct __stat64` and `struct _stat64` as TWO tags with byte-identical members, while mingw-w64's `_mingw_stat64.h` and the UCRT's `sys/stat.h` both reach ONE type through `#define __stat64 _stat64` — and because a descriptor struct interns by NAME plus field types, the identical members did NOT make `_fstat64(_fileno(rv), &x)` compile. Both fixes are config-only: a `symbols` row + seven `constants` rows in `windows.json`, and a `when:{format:pe}` `macros` row replacing the duplicate struct in `sys/stat.json`. ★ RED-ON-DISABLE DIRECTION: a missing declaration is a REFUSED compile, not a wrong answer, so deleting either config row makes this example fail to BUILD — the REMOVE direction a fixture must synthesize. The exit-code arithmetic covers the other failure available here, a declaration that is present but WRONG: `driveFamilyIsTheSdkEnumeration` reds on any wrong constant value and `legacyTagIsOneTypeNotTwo` reds if the alias ever resolved to a different record. ⚠ TWO CELLS ARE TAUTOLOGICAL BY DESIGN AND SAY SO IN THE SOURCE: which drive types a machine has, and whether descriptor 0 is a stat-able handle, are properties of the host — so those cells pin the RANGE of a real call and their contribution is that the call TYPE-CHECKS (the `UINT`-vs-bare-`int` comparison is what exercises the `UINT`->bare-u32 / `LPCWSTR`->ptr<u16> mapping) and that the process survives it. EAGER-IMPORT: `GetDriveTypeW` is a DIRECT named export of the system kernel32.dll (verified by reading the image's export directory — not a forwarder, not absent), so including <windows.h> here cannot repeat the 0xC0000139 class. Every non-pe target compiles the `#else` arm: `windows.json` is `availableObjectFormats:[pe]` and the alias macro is `when:{format:pe}`, so the guarded include is never resolved off pe and elf's genuinely different LFS `struct stat64` is never touched. All four targets exit 42 by two different routes.
